articles.title: Waymo readies autonomous cars for first international tests in Japan
articles.summary: Waymo’s autonomous vehicles are ready to be tested on public roads in Japan. The company is celebrating the milestone of its first international tests.
articles.body: Next week, Waymo’s driverless vehicles will begin testing on public roads in Japan for the Alphabet company’s first international trip. Waymo has yet to confirm whether it will eventually launch a commercial robotaxi service in the country, but the company is still celebrating the excursion as a “significant milestone.” Waymo describes it as a simple “road trip” for collecting data about the nuances of Japanese driving, including left-hand traffic and navigating a dense urban environment. The vehicles will be driven manually for the purposes of gathering mapping data and will be managed by a local taxi fleet operator, Nihon Kotsu. About 25 vehicles are being sent, with the first already having been spotted in a parking lot in Tokyo. As noted by the LinkedIn user who posted the pictures, Waymo’s engineers will have their work cut out for them. Tokyo has its share of idiosyncratic environments, including “tight, winding roads” and thousands of pedestrians and cyclists seamlessly merging with vehicle traffic. Waymo says trained drivers employed by Nihon Kotsu will manually navigate the vehicles across seven central Tokyo wards, including Minato, Shinjuku, Shibuya, Chiyoda, Chūō, Shinagawa, and Kōtō. Waymo operates manually when first arriving in a new city so its engineers can collect data on local traffic patterns and road features. Even though the company’s vehicles have only just arrived, Waymo says it’s already been laying the groundwork, training drivers and fleet managers from GO, a popular taxi app in Japan. The company has also been coordinating with local officials, government agencies, and first responders for the test. “In Tokyo, we are abiding by the same steadfast principles that guide us in the U.S. — commitment to safety, dedication to earning trust in communities where we operate, and collaboration with local officials and community groups here in Tokyo,” said Nicole Gavel, head of business development and strategic partnerships at Waymo, in a statement. Waymo currently operates a commercial robotaxi service in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Austin, with imminent plans to expand to Silicon Valley, Atlanta, Miami, and Washington, DC. The company has also said it will conduct road trip tests in San Diego and Las Vegas. As Waymo tests its vehicles in Japan, the country directly to the west of the island nation is ramping up its own driverless operations. China’s Apollo Go robotaxi service says it completed 1.1 million paid driverless rides in the fourth quarter of 2024 and is expanding to Hong Kong soon. Like Waymo, Apollo Go says it is performing an average of 200,000 paid trips each week.

articles.title: The Google Pixel Watch 4 is the Android watch to beat
articles.summary: The $349.99 Google Pixel Watch 4 adds several smart updates that add up to the best Android smartwatch you can buy.
articles.body: Five years ago, I used to groan when it came time to review an Android smartwatch. Back then, anything that wasn’t a Samsung watch was disappointing at best. The space was fragmented, battery life was dismal, and interest just didn’t seem to be there. But now, the $349.99 Google Pixel Watch 4 is the most interesting flagship smartwatch launch of the season. That wasn’t on my 2025 bingo card. The Pixel Watch 4 may look exactly like the Pixel Watch 3, but it’s a fundamentally different watch. Hardware-wise, the fourth-gen watch is now repairable, features a domed display, and has upgraded specs, like bigger batteries, a new speaker and haptics, and a faster processor. Wear OS 6 adds a complete redesign with Material 3 Expressive, and of course, Gemini is now on the wrist with a new raise-to-talk gesture. On the fitness and health front, sleep tracking is improved, there’s now dual-frequency GPS, and there’s improved automatic activity detection. As for battery life, it lasts longer and charges faster. [Product: Google Pixel Watch 4 | Delightfully wearable The latest Pixel Watch doesn’t upend Google’s design language. It still comes in 41mm and 45mm sizes and looks the same on your wrist. But move closer, and you’ll start seeing the differences. The curve of the domed Actua 360 display is particularly noticeable on the 45mm watch. The bezels are 16 percent thinner, giving you 10 percent more screen real estate. The curve was most noticeable whenever I was scrolling through menus. Google’s Material 3 Expressive software design change is a smart refresh. Tiles hug the edge of the domed display, and animations and buttons are larger with more rounded edges. You can fit more information on a single screen, and the playful design gives the Pixel Watch 4 a more distinctive flavor than before. When paired with a Pixel phone, the devices match each other’s color themes, giving a more cohesive overall vibe. [Image: The battery life is excellent this time around. The display is also brighter, maxing out at 3,000 nits, on par with the Apple Watch Ultra 3. It’s easier to view in direct sunlight. But battery life is the biggest hardware bump this year. Combined with the new power-efficient processors and Wear OS 6’s performance improvements, the watch lasts noticeably longer on a single charge thanks to larger batteries. My colleague Allison Johnson regularly got about a day and a half with the smaller 41mm watch. I’ve been testing the 45mm and got 45 hours on my first full charge. That well exceeds the maximum 32 hours I got on a rundown test of last year’s Pixel Watch 3. I’ve regularly been getting about 36 to 42 hours with the always-on display enabled. It has impressive fast charging, too. I placed the Pixel Watch 4 on the charger at 6:44AM with 14 percent battery. By 7:18AM, I was up to 97 percent. I’m so impressed with the faster charging time that I’m willing to forgive that we now have a third proprietary Pixel Watch charger in four years. Lastly, while I was swapping straps, I was excited to see the screws that let you open up the watch. Wired has an in-depth teardown, but you’ll be able to replace the battery and display yourself. Components will eventually be available through iFixit, and you’ll also be able to get the watch repaired through Google. While we haven’t wrecked a Pixel Watch since the second-gen device, the design is prone to getting banged up. In the past, Google hasn’t done a great job on this front, so this is a welcome development. Gemini is hit or miss I’ve written a bit about Gemini on the wrist this summer. Many of my gripes remain. It’s still not intuitive when you should use it over the phone, multi-step queries have a fair bit of latency, and it’s not always clear how it differs from Google Assistant. That said, the Pixel Watch 4’s implementation of it is sleeker than Samsung’s. The first is the Raise-to-Talk gesture. It’s what it sounds like. You raise your wrist, and Gemini wakes up. You don’t have to make any outlandish Power Ranger-like movements. Raise-to-Talk queries didn’t always work until I tweaked the voice sensitivity options, which are buried in gesture settings. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The revamped Gemini Tile is more useful. You can now save two “shortcuts” to frequent Gemini queries like “summarize my last email” or “turn off all my lights.” (I use the latter daily; the former was not as useful.) There are two other “smart” AI features on the wrist. One is Smart Replies, which offers more personalized replies to your messages. It requires that you’re paired with at least a Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 9 series, or Pixel 10 series phone. However, 95 percent of my text messages are either too long and juicy to use this or are so mundane that typical canned replies are sufficient. Notification cooldown is a new feature that’s supposed to change how frequently you’re notified without needing a do-not-disturb mode. Let’s just say I still get a bazillion notifications from my Nest Doorbell. A better fitness tracker I haven’t gotten to test the new AI-powered Fitbit Health Coach yet. That’s not coming until later this month. But the Pixel Watch 4 has a few notable health and fitness tracking changes. The big one is improved activity detection. The watch will automatically record certain cardio activities for at least 15 minutes. You’ll get a notification and activity recap within an hour of finishing. You can also train the AI to better recognize certain activities over others, like trail runs versus road runs. [Image: There’s a new sleep algorithm too. It was mostly on par with my Oura Ring and Eight Sleep mattress. I tried this for both walks and runs. It accurately recorded activity type and start and end times. I’m bad at tracking walks, so this was a nice perk. Allison also told me that the feature worked well for her cycling sessions. However, this feature doesn’t yet work for anything that isn’t a walk, run, bike ride, spinning, rowing, elliptical, or team sport workout. The Pixel Watch 4 also adds dual-frequency GPS, which is supposed to improve route maps in challenging terrain like cities or dense forests. I was looking forward to this, since Pixel Watch (and Fitbit) GPS maps have historically taken creative licenses with my runs. Across five runs, I noticed a marked improvement. But when compared to the maps of the same runs recorded on the Ultra 3? Fitbit still has some work to do. Emergency satellite SOS is limited to when you’re actually in danger without access to cellular connectivity. Like with the Apple Watch Ultra 3, that wasn’t a scenario I found myself in, despite trekking up three mountains in dense state forests over the past few weeks. You can try a satellite demo (though this doesn’t actually connect you to a satellite), but it’s more helpful to think of this as a backup safety feature than a primary means of emergency communication. [Image: It’s a sleek watch that I’ve enjoyed wearing, even if Gemini is still hit or miss. The AI is great for reminders or turning off smart lights, though. The Android watch to beat For so long, Samsung has been the dominant name in the Android wearable space. But after a relatively static Galaxy Watch 8, I’m confident the Pixel Watch 4 is now the best Android smartwatch in terms of price, feature set, and design. Sure, OnePlus has better overall battery life with its smartwatches. Yeah, Samsung has a physical rotating bezel on the Classic watches. But if I look at which company has the whole package, and a vision about where Android smartwatches should go next? I gotta hand it to Google and the Pixel Watch 4. --- Agree to Continue: Pixel Watch 4 Every smart device now requires you to agree to a series of terms and conditions before you can use it — contracts that no one actually reads. It’s impossible for us to read and analyze every single one of these agreements. But we started counting exactly how many times you have to hit “agree” to use devices when we review them since these are agreements most people don’t read and definitely can’t negotiate. To use the Pixel Watch 4, you must pair it to an Android phone. That means agreeing to that phone’s terms of service and privacy policies. * Google Terms of Service * Google Play Terms of Service * Google Privacy Policy (included in Terms of Service) To use the Fitbit and Fitbit Premium features, there are two mandatory Fitbit agreements: * Fitbit’s Privacy Policy * Fitbit’s Terms of Service Keep in mind that you will be required to log in to Fitbit with your Google account to use the Pixel Watch 4. As part of requirements from global regulators, Google says it must keep your Fitbit health data separate from its Google ads data. Should you choose to integrate any apps with your Fitbit account, like Strava, you will also have to agree to those apps’ terms of service and privacy policies. The same goes if you opt in to Google’s Health Connect API to better integrate with third-party services. Additionally, if you want to use Gemini, you must agree to let Google collect app info and contact info from your devices. Other features like Google Wallet, Google Home, Gmail, Google Calendar, and YouTube Music will also come with their own separate agreements. There will also be several optional permissions related to Bluetooth, location services, and financial services, depending on what you choose to enable. If you choose to activate LTE, you will also have to agree to your carrier’s terms of service and privacy policies. You will have to agree to optional agreements if you choose to use Safety Signal as well. Final tally: five mandatory agreements and a boatload of optional agreements.

articles.title: Samsung’s new 27-inch portable display has a three-hour battery life
articles.summary: The Movingstyle is a 27-inch touchscreen display that features a three hour battery life and can be carried like a giant tablet.
articles.body: Samsung has launched a new portable display that can be pushed around on a rollable stand or carried like a giant tablet. The $1,199.99 Movingstyle is a 27-inch touchscreen display that features a battery life of up to three hours, allowing you to stream content or show workplace presentations without being tied to a power source. The wheeled floorstand includes a height-adjustable arm that can swivel the Movingstyle between landscape and portrait modes, and charges the display when plugged into an outlet. Users can detach the screen from its stand via a sliding button on the back, and carry it around like a briefcase using the built-in handle. That handle also doubles as an adjustable kickstand that can be used to position the Movingstyle on flat surfaces like an artist’s easel, but only in a landscape orientation. Weighing almost 12 pounds without the stand, this won’t be easy for everyone to lug around, but it’s portable enough for users who want to watch movies in their yard or move it between rooms. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The display resolution is 2560 x 1440p, with a 120Hz refresh rate and support for HDR10 Plus and Dolby Atmos audio. The Movingstyle comes with Samsung TV Plus, allowing it to be used like a traditional TV, and Samsung Gaming Hub, which can be used to stream games via Xbox, Nvidia GeForce Now, and Amazon Luna without connecting it to a console. Content can also be streamed via WiFi connectivity, and it supports Bluetooth for linking the Movingstyle to portable speakers or wireless sound systems. [Media: There are ports for two USB-Cs and an HDMI on the back of the screen. Users can navigate the display interface using touchscreen gestures, a remote control it ships with, or via voice commands using Samsung’s Bixby voice assistant. Samsung is also launching a 32-inch 4K Movingstyle model that can’t be removed from its rollable stand. The $699.99 Movingstyle M7 Smart Monitor is remarkably similar to the Moving Style Edge display that Samsung launched in Korea earlier this year, though that model was available in Standard and Lite configurations.

articles.title: KitchenAid redesigned its iconic mixer so you can set an exact speed
articles.summary: KitchenAid’s Artisan Plus Stand Mixer uses a redesigned control lever for precise speed adjustments and adds an LED light, illuminating the inside of the bowl.
articles.body: KitchenAid calls its new Artisan Plus Stand Mixer the biggest upgrade to the appliance since 1955. If you’ve ever been frustrated by the limited speed settings on the brand’s iconic mixers, you might agree. Not only does the new Artisan Plus introduce an additional half-speed setting for gently folding and incorporating ingredients like egg whites and berries, but it also features a redesigned control lever for selecting an exact speed in between its 11 presets. The Artisan Plus Stand Mixer is available from KitchenAid, Williams Sonoma, and other retailers starting today for $599.99 in 11 of the brand’s existing colors, plus four new ones, including sundried tomato, wild blueberry, iron ore bronze, and oat. That’s more expensive than KitchenAid’s $399.99 Classic Series stand mixers, and its more premium $499.99 Artisan Series. The speed control lever is now capped with a knob on the end that can be rotated a quarter-turn to disengage the detents that normally limit its movements to jumping between the 11 presets. The alternate mode allows the lever to smoothly slide up and down the scale, unlocking precise speed adjustments for the mixing tool. While previous versions of the mixer used an electromechanical control system inside, the new Artisan Plus features a microcontroller-based system with a Hall effect sensor for more precision. [Image: A knob on the end of the mixer’s control lever can be turned to unlock precise speed adjustments. Other upgrades include an LED light pointing down into the bowl that KitchenAid fine-tuned with a specific color temperature and intensity to make ingredients look as appetizing as possible. It automatically turns off when the mixer is tilted up, but can be manually activated using the redesigned control lever. The Artisan Plus also comes with a new beater that uses silicone edges to scrape the sides of a bowl as it mixes. It’s only compatible with the new mixer as its upgraded electronics detect the extra friction and increase the motor’s power automatically to maintain the desired speed. articles.title: The 9 biggest new features in Android 17
articles.summary: Android 17 introduces new emoji, AI widgets, and AirDrop for (almost) everyone, all announced at Google’s pre-I/O Android Show.
articles.body: Would it shock you to hear that Android 17 is filled with new AI-enabled features, like improved dictation and vibe-coded widgets? Fortunately, that’s not all. The platform is getting non-AI updates too, from an emoji overhaul to a new screentime tool that helps you avoid distracting apps. Google has just revealed the biggest changes coming in its next OS update as part of its dedicated Android Show, ahead of next week’s big I/O developer conference. The Android software updates came alongside a tease of upcoming Android-powered Googlebook laptops and a host of Android Auto updates. Here are all the new updates that matter and when you can expect them to arrive on your phone. All-new emoji Google has overhauled Android’s emoji set — all 4,000 of them. The new emoji are a little more three-dimensional, with depth and detail lacking in the cartoonish versions they’re replacing. The new emoji will arrive on Pixel phones first, later this year. [Video: Android 17 new emoji] Pause Point This is Google’s latest attempt to inject a little extra digital well-being into the Android experience. Once you label certain apps as “distracting,” Pause Point will pop up anytime you try to open one. It won’t stop you using the app, but it will make you wait through a 10-second timer, with prompts to try breathing exercises or open a more productive app instead — the idea being that it’ll give you a moment to realize you don’t really need to doomscroll Bluesky right now after all. It also lets you set a timer for how long you want to use the app each session, and it has just enough friction to stop you swiping the timer away: It’ll take a full phone restart to turn Pause Point off. [Image: Pause Point lets you set usage timers and do breathing exercises, and it will suggest alternative apps to open. Screen Reactions Google wants to make it easier for budding content creators to put together reaction videos dunking on the rest of the internet. With that in mind, it’s rolling out Screen Reactions, which lets you record video from your selfie camera and what’s on your screen at the same time, all “in just a few taps.” You can record any onscreen content — photos, videos, webpages, and more — and you’ll appear as a cutout in front of it. Screen Reactions will launch on Pixel phones first, sometime this summer. [Image: Google says it will just take “a few taps” to make reaction videos like this. Even more AirDrop After making Android’s Quick Share interoperable with Apple AirDrop late last year on some Pixel and Galaxy phones, Google says support for the feature will roll out more widely this year, including to phones from Xiaomi, Honor, and OnePlus, in addition to already announced support from Oppo and Vivo. For phones that aren’t compatible, starting today Google is adding the ability to use Quick Share to generate a QR code that iPhone users will be able to scan to receive a file directly to their iCloud storage. Later this year, Google says it will add Quick Share and AirDrop support directly into certain apps, including WhatsApp. Easier switching from iPhone Google and Apple have been working together for some time on easier ways to switch from one platform to another. Apple did its part in iOS 26.3, adding support for a new wireless way to transfer files, contacts, messages, homescreen layouts, and eSIMs from an iPhone to an Android device. It still doesn’t actually work, though, because it requires a compatible Android 17 device to transfer all that to. Google says support will finally arrive this year, starting with Pixel and Galaxy phones. Rambler And now the AI stuff. Rambler is one of a few new Android features that Google is branding under “Gemini Intelligence,” and which will roll out to “the latest Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones this summer.” Rambler is one of the more interesting of the bunch. It’s a smart real-time transcription tool that will not only cut out filler words like “um” or “ah” from your speech, but will also make your message more concise and correct any errors. In a demo during a press briefing, Google showed the ability to dictate a shopping list to send in a text message. Rambler not only generated an accurate list, but when the Google rep asked for bananas and then later changed his mind, it knew not to include them at all in the final list. It sounds especially good for the multilingual among us, since it can switch between multiple languages in the same message. [Video: Android 17 Rambler] AI-generated widgets Google must have been impressed by Nothing’s vibe-coded Essential App widgets, because it’s introducing its own take on the concept as another Gemini Intelligence feature. Create My Widget lets you build custom homescreen widgets from natural language. Google suggests a meal planner that recommends protein-heavy recipes, a weather widget for cyclists that prioritizes displaying wind speed and rain, or a live feed of upcoming shows at a local concert venue. Like Rambler, this will come to select Galaxy and Pixel phones this summer. [Video: Android 17 Create My Widget] Gemini automation Alongside Rambler and Create My Widget, Google is updating Android with a host of other new AI automations. Task Automation, already available for food delivery and rideshare apps on the latest Samsung and Google flagships, is getting expanded support for new apps. Google hasn’t detailed which, though it suggests Gemini will be able to order groceries from a shopping list in your notes app or plan a travel itinerary based on a photograph. Chrome auto browse will also come to Android in late June along with a few other AI upgrades for the browser, while Gemini will appear in Autofill to help you complete forms faster. Check out my colleague Allison Johnson’s roundup of Google’s new Android AI announcements for more on what’s in store. More security features Android 17 is also packed with a spread of small security improvements for the platform. Some of these are intended to protect users from scams, like a new collaboration with certain banks to block calls spoofing their number, though it requires you to have their banking app installed. Improved malware detection will scan app behavior for suspicious activity like SMS forwarding or launching in the background, while Chrome’s safe browsing mode will scan app APK downloads for known malware. There are also new protections for when your phone gets stolen: You’ll be able to enable biometric protection remotely when you mark your phone as lost in Find Hub, and Google is reducing the number of attempts someone can make to guess a PIN or password while increasing the wait time between failures.

articles.title: Android 17 arrives on Pixel phones today
articles.summary: Pixel phones get Android 17 first, along with June Pixel Drop features, with other devices getting the OS update later this year.
articles.body: Following its official debut last month, Google is now rolling out Android 17 to compatible Pixel phones, alongside additional exclusive features as part of the June Pixel Drop. Not every feature announced alongside the OS at the pre-I/O Android Show is available today, though. Android 17 itself is arriving on Pixel phones today, and Google says other manufacturers will be issuing the update throughout 2026. The biggest user interface update is the introduction of Bubbles, floating app windows that you can open with a long press — similar floating windows are already found in many Android skins, but are now an official part of 17. Google is making them more useful on bigger screens, with a dedicated “bubble bar” dock at the bottom of the screen for easier multitasking on foldables and tablets. The update also includes Screen Reactions, which make it easy to record selfie video while you screen-record, taking the hassle out of recording a reaction video for social media. Foldables are also getting new gaming controls that display a touchscreen gamepad on the bottom half of the display, while the game itself sits on top, and all Android phones will get native controller remappping. Various expanded parental controls and security features are also included in the update. There are more new features rolling out exclusively to Pixel phones, though most are wider expansions of existing abilities. The new Gemini Omni model will become available in the Gemini app to create video from text prompts, while Lyria 3 lets you do the same for music. AirDrop support through Quick Share is expanding to the Pixel 8A and 9A, Voice Translate for phone calls is coming to the 10A, and Take a Message will now be available on every Pixel from the 6 onward (except in India, where it’s still limited to the 10 series only). Finally, conversational editing in Google Photos is expanding to the UK, Germany, France, Spain, and Italy, while Magic Cue suggestions will appear in new messaging apps — though Google didn’t specify which. There are plenty of features announced at the Android Show that aren’t included in today’s rollout. Google says that its array of new Gemini Intelligence features will arrive on “select advanced devices” later this summer. Those should include the Rambler transcription tool, AI-generated widgets, and expanded Task Automation. Google hasn’t confirmed when other features, like redesigned emoji and the Pause Point well-being tool, will get an official release.

articles.title: Boox is taking on Xteink with its own tiny e-reader
articles.summary: The Boox Picco will be a rival for Xteink’s pocket-size e-readers with a 3.97-inch front-lit display.
articles.body: Boox’s new Tile lineup will take on Xteink’s popular e-readers that are small enough to stick on the back of an iPhone with MagSafe. As spotted by Good E-Reader, the first one is the Picco, which will feature a 3.97-inch front-lit, black-and-white e-paper display and expandable storage with an SD card slot. Boox confirmed to The Verge that the Picco is in the works, noting that it’s part of a new Tile lineup and will have an “accessible price point,” but without any other details about its plans, like specs, the specific price, or a release date. The front-lit display could put it on par with Xteink’s new $99 X4 Pro e-reader, which The Verge’s Andrew Liszewski calls “the best tiny e-reader you can buy.” However, part of the appeal of Xteink’s little e-readers is their ability to magnetically stick to the back of a phone, and it’s not clear yet if the Boox Picco will have a similar feature. [Media: It appears to have buttons in a promotional image, but it’s also not clear yet if it will rely solely on buttons, like the original Xteink X4, or also include a touchscreen. According to Good E-Reader, the Picco will likely have a minimal, tiled UI limited to basic apps like Neoreader, a music player, and a podcast player, putting it in a very different category than the Android-powered Boox Palma.

articles.title: The Dell XPS 13 is the first real competitor to the MacBook Neo
articles.summary: Even the base XPS 13 is an excellent laptop. But you’re still gonna want the 16GB model.
articles.body: Dell’s last XPS 13 was meant to be a farewell before the company sunset the entire XPS brand. But it was a bitter ending, and an overpriced one as well. Earlier this year, Dell resurrected the XPS name with the excellent (and very expensive) XPS 14 and 16. And now, it’s reinvented the XPS 13 as a much more affordable thin-and-light to take on the MacBook Neo. Call it another comeback. The 2026 XPS 13 has the nicest hardware you’ll find in a new $700 laptop outside of Apple’s Neo. The core components — the screen, keyboard, trackpad, and speakers — are all great or excellent. It’s an exquisite package in a sleek and very thin ultra-portable. And unlike other Windows 11 laptops that struggled to get by with 8GB of RAM, the XPS 13 feels competent even with that limited memory allocation. But even though it’s great that there’s an 8GB Windows laptop in 2026 that’s not dead on arrival, you’re still going to want the 16GB version (which I’ve also been testing) for $1,000. And sadly, no configuration of the XPS 13 includes a headphone jack. [Product: Dell XPS 13 (2026) | I’ve been testing two XPS 13 configurations with the same six-core Intel Core 5 320 “Wildcat Lake” processor and 512GB SSD. Their singular difference is memory: The base $799.99 model has 8GB of RAM and the $999.99 one has 16GB. I’ve been working off this pair quite a bit for a couple weeks, and the hardware is brilliant. When I got them, that 8GB / 512GB configuration was the base model and cost $699.99. But in early September, Dell created a new $699.99 base model with just 256GB of storage, and raised the price of the 512GB models by $100 each. Sadly these kinds of pricing shenanigans are commonplace in our ongoing RAMageddon nightmare. --- Component report card * Screen: A * Webcam: A * Keyboard: B * Trackpad: B * Port selection: D * Speakers: B * Number of ugly stickers to remove: 1 --- The XPS 13 is the nicest-looking and -feeling Windows laptop you’re going to find at this price. It’s just as sleek as a MacBook Neo or Air, and at 2.2 pounds / 1kg and 0.5 inches / 12.7mm thick, it’s lighter than the Air and almost as thin. The XPS is an exquisite laptop to hold, and it practically disappears into a bag. The screen has much thinner bezels than a Neo, and it’s equally bright and colorful — but with 120Hz refresh and touch support rather than the Neo’s 60Hz non-touch screen. It even has an anti-glare finish the Neo doesn’t offer. The speakers sound surprisingly good for such a compact laptop, offering a well-rounded sound that gets plenty loud. The mechanical trackpad is small, even shorter than the Neo’s, but its only major downside is that it doesn’t physically click in all four corners. Even the webcam impressed me, rendering very good color and handling poor light or backlighting just fine. And the keyboard? Somebody tell Dell’s designers to put this nice tactile chiclet-style keyboard on everything and give up on that latticeless look on other XPS laptops. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Battery life and thermals aren’t amazing, but they’re adequate. The bottom chassis frequently warms your lap, with its hottest point reaching as high as 104 degrees Fahrenheit / 40 degrees Celsius, but the keyboard deck stays cool. As for the battery, it typically got me seven hours of continuous mixed usage (lots of Chrome tabs, a few video calls, and streaming a few albums with the screen on most of the time) or up to 10 hours during a much lighter meeting-free day. I’d usually prefer a thicker laptop for the sake of more battery, but I’ve been smitten enough by the XPS’s small and light frame to feel this is passable — even though the Neo lasts several hours longer on an even lower-capacity battery. The XPS 13 has two 10Gbps USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports, one on either side, and both support charging and video-out. But why, oh why, does this laptop not have a headphone jack? Even if you rarely use 3.5mm audio it’s nice to have as a fallback option. As for raw performance, both versions of the XPS 13 fall well behind the MacBook Neo’s A18 Pro in synthetic benchmark tests like Geekbench, though the 16GB model is significantly closer in our Premiere 4K export test. And the XPS’s six-core Wildcat Lake chip is night-and-day better than the five-core version found in the Chuwi UniBook, which took over an hour to export. The extra performance core and extra GPU core in the XPS 13 make a notable difference, and so does its speedy storage. The XPS 13’s SSD read speed is nearly three times as fast as the Chuwi, and nearly four times as fast as the Neo. In day-to-day use of the XPS 13, 8GB of RAM actually feels passable, unlike with the Chuwi and recent Surface Laptop 13-inch. I have used it without any major failings or crashes, and it’s mostly gotten by okay when all I ask of it is simple web-based stuff. But having only 8GB of memory does occasionally slow you down while multitasking. For example, with a dozen or more Chrome tabs open on it I occasionally had to wait for my tabs to reload when I switched back and forth between them. That’s a normal Chrome feature to save memory, but it happens a lot on the 8GB XPS 13. And when I was bouncing between a couple dozen Chrome tabs and messaging colleagues on Slack — not an unusual workload — even tabs I had used just minutes before got dumped from memory and needed to reload. [Image: I dig that the XPS branding is back. The last XPS 13 just had the boring Dell logo on the lid. I was working late one night, writing up some recent news, and slowly getting frustrated as those split-second delays added up. Switching tabs, swiping between virtual desktops, swiping up into Windows’ Task View — it all worked, but every so often the swipes and quick changes felt a little slower. I then made the mistake of opening Adobe Photoshop to do a few simple image crops, and I suddenly regretted life itself. It was the kind of edit that normally takes me a couple minutes, but every little drop-down menu or drag-and-drop in Photoshop felt excruciatingly slow. These are the ways you still feel the friction of 8GB of RAM on Windows, even in an otherwise brilliant laptop. The 16GB XPS 13 doesn’t have those same pain points — not at this workload, at least. Going up to 16GB of RAM gives you adequate headroom so Windows isn’t constantly trying to reallocate memory, and you can actually do the occasional demanding task like opening and resizing an unexpectedly large image file. The XPS’s speedy SSD seems to help compared to other 8GB laptops I’ve used recently, but you know what helps even more? More RAM. It’s just a shame you’re paying an extra $300 to get it in the 16GB / 512GB XPS 13 config, which now costs $999.99 — it was a $200 upcharge mere weeks ago. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: While the MacBook Neo is still the clear winner in performance, the XPS 13 is its best competition yet. Dell has positioned this as an affordable student laptop, just like the Neo, and the company has mostly nailed it — at least in the US, where the XPS 13 seems to be much cheaper than in other regions (sorry, international friends). The models with 8GB RAM are even the same price as the Neo, at $699.99 for 265GB of storage and $799.99 for 512GB. At the time of this review, Dell still offers a $100 discount for high school and college students, matching Apple’s education discount on the Neo. But the promo is temporary, whereas Apple’s own $100 student discount has no set expiration. You could still save much more with a laptop like the HP OmniBook 3 that I just reviewed, getting you more RAM, more ports, better battery life, slightly more performance (except in graphics), and a much bigger screen for only $500-ish — but it’s a bulkier laptop that doesn’t feel or look remotely as nice as the XPS 13. The MacBook Neo has jump-started new competition in this $700-ish laptop space, all while RAMageddon rages on and makes everything more expensive (including the Neo itself). We’re about to see even more laptop makers launch their answers to the Neo, and hopefully that means more great, affordable choices — for students or just about anyone in need. The XPS 13 is the frontrunner of MacBook Neo competitors for now, and it shows that an 8GB Windows laptop can actually work okay. articles.title: macOS 27 is available now
articles.summary: Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate on Monday, bringing the new Siri AI assistant, Liquid Glass improvements, improved performance, and more. The update is compatible with all Macs with Apple Silicon, but no Intel Macs.
articles.body: Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate on Monday, which brings the new Siri AI assistant, Liquid Glass improvements, improved performance, and more. The update is compatible with all Macs with Apple Silicon, but not Intel Macs — Apple released its final big update for Intel-based Macs last year with macOS Tahoe. Siri AI is arguably the biggest feature in macOS 27, and it allows you to ask questions, search through things involving your personal context like photos and emails, and take actions in apps such as Messages and Reminders. There’s a new dedicated Siri app that keeps an archive of your chats for easier reference. However, Siri AI will initially launch as a beta and will only be available in English. As for Liquid Glass, Apple says the update offers “uniform refraction and improved contrast,” and there is a new slider that makes Liquid Glass elements more or less opaque. And there’s one other major UI change worth celebrating: consistent window corner radii.

articles.title: Mikayla Matthews Quits ‘Secret Lives Of Mormon Wives’: “There’s No Amount Of Money Worth Going Against My Morals”
articles.summary: Mikayla Matthews is leaving The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives amid turmoil in MomTok. The influencer and Hulu star shared the news in a social media post as t...
articles.body:
Mikayla Matthews is leaving The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives amid turmoil in MomTok.

The influencer and Hulu star shared the news in a social media post as the cast was recently seen in Italy filming Season 6 of the reality series.

"I made my decision over a week ago, after hearing some news, that I will not be continuing the show at this moment," Matthews posted on Instagram. "I've said from the beginning of this that I'm not comfortable being a part of something that continues to platform behavior I don't agree especially given my own experience growing up in a home with multiple forms of abuse."

She continued, "There's no amount of money worth going against my morals or changing the stance I've had since I first saw and heard the things that made me feel this strongly. And for me personally, continuing to directly profit from this behavior feels wrong and unethical. It feels like a disservice to the children, everyone's healing and the millions of people watching."

Matthews is seemingly referring to her co-star Taylor Frankie Paul, whose personal life has been at the center of drama on Secret Lives of Mormon Wives since the first season. Production for Season 5 of the series was paused after domestic violence allegations from Paul's ex, Dakota Mortensen, with whom she shares a child. Legal actions, a custody battle, and an old resurfaced video showing Paul physically assaulting Mortensen were released ahead of the release of The Bachelorette , which prompted ABC to cancel its premiere.

On the most recent season of SLOMW , Matthews and Paul clashed over the latter not wanting any criticism of her life. Although Matthews and Paul mended things on camera, things off-camera didn't seem to be good.

Matthews points out that the children ultimately suffer from continuing to expose their troubling lives on camera. Hulu will seemingly continue to work with Paul, which Matthews doesn't think is good for her mental health or for the rest of the cast and their children.

"This show has been a huge part of my life and has helped me provide for my family," Matthews continued. "I'm so grateful for the experience, and will continue sharing my story, my health and advocating for myself and others this shouldn't be 'relatable' or entertainment in anyway. Supporting an ADULT doesn't mean constantly making excuses for toxic behavior while giving unconditional sympathy and grace with zero accountability or change. I was in that enabling cycle for years, and I'm not going to be a part of that again! love you all."

articles.title: Apple Home’s new security camera features cost up to $60 a month
articles.summary: Apple Intelligence upgrades to HomeKit Secure Video come with a steep cost.
articles.body: With the public release of iOS 27 and tvOS 27, Apple Home is getting an injection of Apple Intelligence — but you’ll have to pay more for it. Apple Intelligence for Home brings AI-powered video summaries to HomeKit Secure Video, so you can get short text descriptions of who and what compatible security cameras saw, along with the clip. It also adds a new video search feature and the ability to stitch footage from multiple cameras into one clip, making it easier to keep an eye on what’s happening around your home without scrolling through footage. [Image: AI-generated video summaries provide text descriptions of what a camera sees. But to get these features, you’ll need to pay $9.99 a month for the 2TB iCloud Plus plan (or $39.95 a month for an Apple One Premier subscription) — and that’s just for one camera. According to an Apple support page, to add Apple Intelligence to a second camera, you’ll have to pay $29.99 a month for the 6TB plan. For up to five cameras, it’s a whopping $59.99 a month for the 12TB plan. No word on whether you can add more than five cameras. (Recordings from HomeKit-connected cameras don’t count toward your storage quota.) That’s way too expensive. While the improved video features are useful — I’ve been testing them in beta and have been impressed — they’re not good enough to justify that big a price jump. HomeKit Secure Video has always been behind a paywall, but it started at a very reasonable $1 a month. That’s for the 50GB iCloud Plus plan, which includes recorded footage from one camera, plus smart alerts and facial recognition. For more cameras, you bump up to 2TB / $9.99 a month (up to five), and 6TB / $29.99 a month or higher for unlimited cameras. But the cost for the Apple Intelligence features is a huge increase. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I currently pay $40 a month for Apple One Premier, which includes 2TB of iCloud storage and gets me HomeKit Secure Video support for five cameras. With the new pricing tier, I keep those benefits and now get Apple Intelligence on one camera. But to get it on all five cameras, I’d need to pay an additional $60 a month. That’s $720 a year, for a total of $1,200. Amazon’s Ring and Google Nest charge around $20 a month for subscription tiers that include similar AI-powered features for their cameras, and both companies offer more features than Apple currently does. An iCloud Plus plan does include storage for photos, files, and device backups, and higher plans may get you higher limits for Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features, but Apple hasn’t released any details about that. The good news is that none of this changes what you get with HomeKit Secure Video today, and the new software releases have added under-the-hood upgrades that improve speed and reliability, plus the service now supports 4K video resolution. But while Apple Intelligence feels like a significant improvement for Apple Home, at these prices, the value just isn’t there. Screenshots by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Jensen Huang made headlines Monday at the All-In conference in L.A. when President Trump called him, live, on stage. But there was something else worth noting about his appearance. Huang, dressed in his now-signature alligator leather jacket, was handed a foldable phone to answer it.

articles.title: 'Widow's Bay' won big, Mariska nailed it and Taylor Swift spoofed 'SVU': The 2026 Emmys, from every angle
articles.summary: From Mariska Hargitay's many outfit changes to Zendaya and Tom Holland's charm offensive, the Emmys delivered all around.
articles.body:
What a night, eh? Emmys host Mariska Hargitay presided over an evening of laughs, tears (Noah Kahan singing "Bridge Over Troubled Water" during the In Memoriam? Pass the tissues.) and Taylor Swift. To break down TV's biggest night, we enlisted our best experts — from our resident TV critic to style pros to internet culture vultures to boots-on-the-ground correspondents reporting live from the red carpet and press room.

Here's what they'll remember most from the 2026 Emmys — good and bad.

Cutest couple goes to Zendaya and Tom Holland

There's something refreshing about an A-list, box-office star who has absolutely no problem being the plus-one. Of course, when your plus-one is your wife, Zendaya, it's a pretty great gig. Tom Holland came to the Emmys on Monday night simply to support Zendaya, who was nominated for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for the third and final season of Euphoria .

While she walked the red carpet solo, Holland quietly slipped inside — but once the show started, the famously low-key couple wasn't exactly hard to spot. Holland enthusiastically cheered Zendaya on when her category was announced, even though the award ultimately went to Rhea Seehorn. And throughout the night, the two seemed perfectly content, making the Emmys their own very glamorous date night.

They caught up with friends, including Ayo Edebiri, and shared a particularly sweet moment with Mark Ruffalo, laughing together before Zendaya and Holland each pulled him in for a hug. For two of the biggest movie stars in the world, they somehow still give off the energy of a couple who are just genuinely happy to be hanging out together. No grand red carpet couple moment required.

Taryn Ryder , senior entertainment reporter

Matthew Rhys was definitely the most popular celeb of the night. Are we even surprised, though? He took home two awards and was a total crowd-pleaser in the press room, where I was stationed for the night. He readily gushed over Widow's Bay executive producer and director Hiro Murai when I asked him about balancing horror and comedy and quipped about having a playful rivalry with his partner, The Diplomat star Keri Russell, who was also nominated tonight. When he was told his time was up, he genuinely seemed bummed out. He loved chatting with us, and we loved chatting with him!

Neia Balao , entertainment and lifestyle reporter

This awards season is picking up where last year's left off: Feathers are still very much the moment. They were everywhere, from neckline trims, like the pink layers on Allison Janney's black gown and the feather effect on Nicole Kidman's snowy Chanel dress, to full-length fringe, like Jaclyn Smith's seafoam number. It's a trend I'm already adding to my own cart, if I'm being honest.

Nineties fashion isn't the only thing making a comeback — the decade's hair is having its own little reunion tour, and nowhere was that clearer than during tonight's ceremony. Rachel Sennott was among a handful of attendees who went sky-high with their ponytails in a way that was pure '90s slumber party-energy. Meanwhile, Florence Pugh showed up in a spiky, piecey updo that was bold, delightfully unhinged and gave me slight prom-war flashbacks. (A cosmic force may have added some styling paste to my cart right now.) Now, the style isn't something that would work on just anybody, but Pugh obviously pulls it off.

Elsewhere on the red carpet, the throwbacks kept coming, just less obviously '90s. There were some teasing, some slicked-back buns and sleek middle parts, though Shailene Woodley's low, center ponytail had more of a 1970s cult energy. (Is there a Manson family film somewhere on the horizon that I don't know about?) However, it still tracks since the actual '90s were never just about one overarching look. The decade swung from grunge to glam to minimalism to maximalism, so it makes sense that tonight didn't settle on a single '90s archetype either.

The Emmys carpet may be blue, but this year's looks were red-hot. Host Mariska Hargitay stunned in floor-length sequins in a screaming five-alarm red that would probably make Jessica Rabbit do a double-take. Plenty more stunned in similarly bold tones, including Niecy Nash-Betts, Brooks Nader, Jessica Belkin, Cailee Spaeny, Rhea Seehorn and Jackie Tohn, while even more embraced a rich burgundy, including Taylor Dearden, Fiona Dourif, Calista Flockhart and Cynthia Nixon, who was deemed "best dressed" by E!'s Keltie Knight early in the night for her asymmetrical textured Issey Miyake gown. The good news: You don't have to spend a bundle to channel her look.

There's been some talk on the internet lately about whether red lips are "outdated" — an argument I don't think holds up when red lips have been a look for literal centuries. The Emmys proved that a crimson mouth goes beyond any trend cycle. Cailee Spaeny and Jackie Tohn were refreshingly unafraid to go full makeup-monotone, matching their red lips to their gowns, while Dakota Fanning and Emmy Rossum used theirs as a pop of color instead. One thing that's always worked in red lipstick's favor? There are plenty of drugstore formulas that perform just as well as the high-end ones. (I should know, I have all of them!)

For those who prefer something more understated, nudes were the other lip look all over the ceremony. Odessa A'zion, Zendaya and Kristen Bell were among the stars who went the subtle route. It's also just as easy — a defined lip liner and a swipe of gloss can get you that same look without committing to a full matte neutral.

I'll never not love an outfit that's basically encrusted in gems , so it's no surprise that my favorite looks of the night were the big swings that landed, especially the sculptural gowns with 3D effects that toed the line between architecture and fashion. My top picks: Selena Gomez's Louis Vuitton dress that looked like it was constructed with stacks of gold bricks, Zendaya's custom Prada gown that literally dripped in gems and Chase Infiniti's Louis Vuitton mermaid gown that evoked a web of copper bubbles woven together. BTW, Linda Cardellini has never looked better than she does tonight in a mother-of-pearl tiled gown by Yara Shoemaker.

My favorite look of the night goes to Elle Fanning, who was nominated for Margo's Got Money Trouble s. She wore a strappy, jade-green Ralph Lauren gown with a dramatic train and delicate tassel detailing, with a muted red lip and her blond hair in loose curls. Is the energy fairy or mermaid? Either way, I love it. That sort of mint-jade green is an unexpected and underrated red carpet color that always gets my attention. And the fact that she paired it with platforms in the same jade shade instead of gold or silver is a real power move. Brava!

Well, that was a long night for Mariska Hargitay, who seemed to live an entirely new life with every costume change during her duties as Emmys host. When she arrived on the red carpet in a Jessica Rabbit-inspired red sequin gown, I thought that she couldn't possibly look any better. And then she did — in the silver strapless gown she wore to take the stage for her opening monologue. And again in black satin with gold embellishments. And then came pink sequins, followed by a black strapless gown with leather gloves.

There was her Game of Thrones look, which she was admittedly sweating through, before she changed into — what else? — another stunning sequin dress. If you're having trouble keeping up, that brings us to seven looks. There were still four more to come. Making the whole thing even more confusing — and impressive — were the drastic hair transformations between outfits. Over the course of the three-hour show, Hargitay went from mid-length beachy waves to cascading Old Hollywood curls and, ultimately, a chin-length bob. Naturally, she pulled off every version flawlessly and made the whole production look effortless. Now I'm left with two questions: What exactly was happening backstage to make all that glam possible? And has anyone checked on her styling team?

Kerry Justich , senior lifestyle reporter

Mariska Hargitay makes the case for a comedic role

Though we know and love her as the stern cop with a heart of gold, Olivia Benson, Mariska Hargitay showed that she has comedic chops too. She had me rolling on the floor with her jokes about Dick Wolf and the number of Emmys she's won for Law and Order: Special Victims Unit. Zero is a number!

My personal favorite joke came during her monologue, when she referenced Nicole Kidman's iconic AMC Theaters ad — and when Kidman responded, Hargitay ordered her to "zip it, movie lady."

I also have to give a shoutout to Jalen Brunson's appearance in Hargitay's opening number. He'll also be making his comedic debut soon, when he hosts Saturday Night Live later this month.

Kelsey Weekman , senior entertainment reporter

There were predictable yet deserving wins like The Pitt , Jean Smart and Stephen Colbert, but there were also more unexpected wins than usual: Sally Field for the straight-to-streaming Netflix film Remarkably Bright Creatures, Allison Janney for The Diplomat , Tom Pelphrey for Task and Slow Horses in directing, to name a few. It's possible that vote splitting contributed to some of these surprises, especially given the many nominations for The Pitt. On this, I say competition is healthy, and an upset is always more exciting than straight-across sweep domination.

Michel Ghanem, Trust Me, I Watch Everything TV critic and writer behind TV Scholar

One such surprise became the highlight of the evening: Apple TV's word-of-mouth horror-comedy hit Widow's Bay . The entertaining series follows the mayor of a small island off the coast of New England as he tries his best to revitalize it for tourism, despite one big problem: it's haunted. Historically, the Emmys have not been kind to horror. Some of the highlights of the genre, like The Haunting of Hill House , were previously completely shut out. The infusion of comedy into Widow's Bay made it stand out as something unique, and it's also possible recent sci-fi shows like Severance helped open the door for Emmy voters to consider more fantastical options (rather than a grounded comedy like Margo's Got Money Troubles ). Widow's Bay is walking away with the most awards of the night.

It's too bad to see a show like Love Story walk away empty-handed ( DTF St. Louis was pretty much a guaranteed win after Linda Cardellini and David Harbour snagged wins last weekend at the Creative Arts ceremony for their supporting roles).

Finally, when we step back and look at the overall winning slate, a worrying pattern emerges: Not a single actor of color was awarded tonight. Hollywood, especially after 2020, made a concerted push to commission more stories at the margins and cast in a representative way. This year's wins feel like the official end of that era, in a way. Each of tonight's winners is talented — but it's a concerning trend of the kinds of shows being greenlit and highlighted more broadly, and something I'll be keeping an eye on as a critic.

Meg Stalter delivers the standout red carpet look — again

Never one to miss a chance to reference something funny on the red carpet, nominee Meg Stalter stole the pre-show by dressing up in gold and body paint to resemble an Emmy statuette.

She committed to the bit, wearing the body paint to the ceremony as well, where she cheered on costar Jean Smart as she won the award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series. I have to wonder if the chair she's been sitting in all night has turned gold too.

In the past, Stalter has dressed as Kylie Jenner (to Paul W. Downs's Timothée Chalamet), a coffee cup and Diet Coke . I loved it when she wore a basic white tee and jeans to last year's Emmys.

Taylor Swift makes a surprise appearance (and drops some Easter eggs)

I have to apologize to everyone I scoffed at when they asked if Taylor Swift would be at the Emmys because technically she was, even though she was physically at her husband's football game, hanging out with Tom Cruise.

Swift made an appearance in a pre-taped sketch, in which she plays a detective helping the cast of Law and Order: Special Victims Unit try to figure out … well, whether Taylor Swift was coming to the Emmys. Classic conundrum.

I should have known she'd do a favor for her pal Mariska Hargitay — one of Swift's cats is named after Hargitay's iconic character, Olivia Benson, and that's a bond far stronger than marriage.

Since she can only ever be herself, Swift joked about her penchant for Easter eggs and her fans' passion for decoding them — while dropping a few herself. Does anyone know what " saccharide, Aeries, from the vineyard, north or south " means?

articles.body:
However, there were plenty more moments that took place inside the Peacock Theater that you may have missed. From Tom Holland's sneaky appearance to Carrie Coon being the ultimate Rhea Seehorn fangirl to plenty of costar reunions, here are the best behind-the-scenes moments from the Emmy Awards.

Jean Smart introduces her 18-year-old son, Forrest Gilliland, to Mariska Hargitay during a moment of downtime.

Martin Short and Dan Levy, who both shared close relationships with the late Catherine O'Hara, appear to comfort each other during the show. Levy was one of her three onscreen children — in addition to Macaulay Culkin and Annie Murphy — who paid tribute to her during the In Memoriam segment .

Tom Holland skipped the carpet but was spotted greeting fellow attendees inside the show, where he showed up to support his wife (or is she?) Zendaya , who was nominated for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for her role in Euphoria.

Former Ozark costars Julia Garner and Jason Bateman hung out with Carrie Coon during the show.

From a witchy weekend to an angelic Emmys appearance, Nicole Kidman looked ethereal as always.

Big Little Lies costars Nicole Kidman and Shailene Woodley caught up during a commercial break.

Has national intelligence been compromised?! Keri Russell appears to deliver a startling piece of news to her Diplomat costar Allison Janney, as Rufus Sewell and his wife Vivian Benitez also take it all in.

articles.title: Volvo’s plug-in hybrid XC60 and XC90 can really go the distance
articles.summary: Volvo’s plug-in hybrid XC60 and XC90 are getting bigger batteries for longer electric ranges. New styling and Google’s Gemini are also coming to these models.
articles.body: Most plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV) today get an average of around 30–50 miles of battery-only range: decent, but not mind-blowing. With hybrid sales dominating the market today, Volvo is out to prove that its PHEVs can push the limits of what’s possible. Today, the Swedish automaker revealed the updated PHEV versions of its popular XC60 and XC90 SUVs are its first “long range plug-in hybrids,” delivering class-leading ranges of 78 miles and 73 miles, respectively. That’s more than double the electric range of previous PHEV variants. The numbers are still preliminary and based on EPA testing standards. But if confirmed, they would make Volvo’s PHEVs “the longest electric range of any plug-in hybrids available in the American market,” the automaker claims. Volvo took a page from its all-electric vehicle design by integrating the battery directly in the floor of both vehicles for improved efficiency. The batteries are also higher capacity — 41.2 kWh (37.9 kWh usable) for both — and able to send more energy to the motors, which are also more powerful. [Image: [Image: [Image: Of course, those batteries are just dead weight if owners forget to charge them — which tends to happen with a lot of plug-in hybrids. Hybrid owners often neglect to charge, thanks to the gas tank that continues to power their vehicle even with a dead battery. Still, the higher capacity batteries in the XC60 and XC90 are sure to appeal to a lot of car shoppers who may still like the sound of increased range even if they don’t exactly plan on taking full advantage of it. The XC60 is getting new styling to bring it inline with Volvo’s new design language. That includes an upgraded grille, redesigned front bumper, hood, front wings, rear bumper, tailgate, new wheel designs, and a refined “Thor’s Hammer” LED headlight light signature. Like the redesigned XC40, the XC60 also has a more expansive driver assist that includes Automatic Emergency Steering and Braking, collision prevention, and a door-opening cyclist alert. The addition of Google’s Gemini chatbot as the new voice assistant rounds everything out. Volvo was one of the first automakers to adopt Google’s software for its infotainment systems, so naturally that now includes Gemini. Production on the XC60 and XC90 begins late Fall 2026, with customer deliveries scheduled to begin in early 2027. Volvo is hoping that a boost in hybrid sales can help fund its future pure EV models, like the EX50, EX60, and new affordable model that will replace the EX30.

articles.title: Microsoft issues emergency Windows 11 update to fix its record-breaking patch
articles.summary: The out-of-band update fixes Remote Desktop, USB audio, and Hyper-V issues.
articles.body: Microsoft has started rolling out an emergency out-of-band update to fix problems with its record-breaking September patch Tuesday update. The software giant patched nearly 1,000 flaws in its biggest update ever this month, but it also introduced some bugs that have affected businesses, developers, and gamers. The September patch Tuesday affected folder shares on Hyper-V-based Linux virtual machines, Remote Desktop Services sessions, and some USB audio devices. Microsoft’s out-of-band update, released yesterday, addresses these issues across Windows 11 versions 26h1, 25H2, and 24H2. Microsoft has also released updates for Windows Server 2025 and 2022, the LTSC versions of Windows 10, and Windows Server 2012 and Windows Server 2012 R2. In the past it was unusual for Microsoft to issue out-of-band updates to Windows, but it has become far more common this year. In January, the company was forced to issue four out-of-band updates after a buggy Windows 11 patch. In March, the company then had to issue two emergency updates because of installation failures and Microsoft account sign-in problems. Microsoft also released an out-of-band update in July to address an Intel driver issue that was causing performance issues and battery drain.

articles.title: GM updates its trucks’ native software to coexist with CarPlay
articles.summary: GM is introducing a new user interface for its Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks that includes, for the first time, picture-in-picture phone projection.
articles.body: General Motors is polishing up the software experience in its bestselling trucks in an effort to reduce the amount of dangerous tapping and swiping that’s required to access the most-used controls. It’s also giving Apple CarPlay and Android Auto spiffy new picture-in-picture displays — which is notable given GM’s previously stated hostility to phone mirroring in its electric vehicles. When the next-generation interface makes its debut on the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 later this year, vehicle owners will see a number of changes, including slick new graphics for its advanced driver-assist system, animated transitions between displays, and simplified layouts for heavy-duty truck stuff like trailering and off-roading. And they’ll be seeing it all on 60-plus inches of screen real estate — the combined size of instrument cluster, central display, and passenger screen in some of its trucks — that’s designed to enhance but not overwhelm the driving experience. For GM, larger displays do not necessarily mean more distractions. Instead, the automaker views the additional space as an opportunity to be smarter about how information is presented and to make interactive elements larger, said Colin McCormick, group product manager for Google built-in, projection, and profiles at GM. Larger buttons and bigger tap zones can make the system easier to operate, particularly under difficult driving conditions, he said. “The buttons can be larger and make it easier to do,” McCormick said. “Living in Michigan, the roads are terrible, so I’m trying to tap on a very small tap zone while hitting a bunch of potholes. These larger displays give you better functionality in that standpoint.” [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: There are still plenty of physical buttons for key functions like HVAC. But when you want to control the direction of the airflow, a new menu appears as a flyout. Customers have repeatedly professed their love for physical controls, so GM understands that moving key functions onto the screen just because there’s more real estate doesn’t necessarily earn them any goodwill. There are some formerly tangible tools that are now becoming digital only. The oil dipstick, for example, is now a virtual measurement that exists on the truck’s status screen. But the majority of the physical touchpoints remain physical. Borrowing from the world of smartphone design, GM’s designers added a swipe-down notification interface for quick access to functions such as switching connected devices, entering settings, and privacy controls. Truck owners can disable the vehicle’s microphone directly from this interface, for example. The new interface also distinguishes between settings, which vehicle owners will likely visit once and then rarely ever again, and controls, which they may want to tweak more frequently. GM wanted to address the complaint that its existing interface can feel disjointed because various functions abruptly take over the entire display, McCormick said. So rather than constantly replacing the entire screen, displays such as the media player can remain visible while an additional queue panel slides in from the side. By using animated transitions, the automaker is hoping to create a more contextual experience when moving between functions. Lots of truck owners love to haul trailers, so GM put a particular focus on that experience with its new software designs. Trailering information now appears both in the driver information display and in the smaller homescreen card. The trucks include built-in trailer-aware navigation, so once a trailer is connected, the vehicle identifies it, and Google Maps can provide a route that accommodates the trailer. Customers enter the trailer’s dimensions, and those measurements can be carried from one vehicle to another through the customer’s GM account. [Image: But it’s when using Apple CarPlay or Android Auto that Chevy and GMC truck owners may see the most noticeable differences. Again, engineers were hoping to use the added screen real estate “intelligently,” McCormick said. And they didn’t want phone projection to completely take over the truck’s native infotainment, nor did they want to force customers to choose between them. The solution: picture-in-picture phone mirroring, in which CarPlay and Android Auto occupy a large contextual card rather than taking over the entire screen. When a phone is connected through CarPlay, the phone icon changes into a CarPlay icon; selecting it brings up CarPlay within that large card. Pressing the native home button returns the driver to the split-screen home view. This allows customers to use Apple’s apps while retaining access to native GM functions, like trailering info. The new layout is even more interesting when you consider GM’s seismic decision in 2023 to drop Apple CarPlay and Android from its EVs. Despite pushback from customers, GM has stood by its decision, arguing that it can deliver a better software experience to its customers without phone mirroring. GM CEO Mary Barra even suggested (in an interview on Decoder) the ban would eventually extend to the automaker’s gas-powered trucks and SUVs — only to walk it back days later. That’s left GM to tweak CarPlay and Android Auto’s appearance in its Chevy and GMC trucks to enable the native GM-branded software experience to peek through. Phone projection will no longer occupy the entire screen, which McCormick argues was forcing drivers to dangerously switch back and forth when they needed to access their truck’s native controls. In this way, truck owners can choose to project their phone while also accessing key information, like trailering or off-roading details, McCormick said. “I think we’re landing in a spot where… we don’t have a customer that has to decide, ‘Oh, I’m going to use projection, or, oh, I want to use the native system,’” he said. “That’s our sweet spot.” The new UI will roll out to new Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks later this year, but only to new customers. Existing owners will be stuck with the previous-generation experience. The goal was to put the new interface on GM’s “bread-and-butter” trucks rather than first introducing it on lower-volume vehicles, which is more typical for a new experience, McCormick said. GM is so confident in the system that it’s launching it on its bestselling trucks so it can get in front of as many customers as possible. GM sells close to 900,000 of these trucks a year, meaning the company expects to receive a substantial amount of feedback once the new interface is live and being used by customers. Some aspects of the first version may work extremely well, while others may need to be changed. ”We’ll take that experience, and the OTAs will allow us to get there,” McCormick said.

articles.title: Matthew Rhys just made Emmys history. He didn't thank Keri Russell onstage, but backstage was a different story.
articles.summary: After a record-setting Emmys night, 'Widow's Bay' star Rhys saved his most personal praise for his longtime partner and fellow nominee.
articles.body:
Matthew Rhys won big at Monday night's 2026 Emmys. The Welsh actor made history by becoming the first person to win two lead acting Emmys in the same year, taking home awards for his starring roles in Netflix's limited series The Beast in Me and Apple TV comedy Widow's Bay .

He also picked up a third award as an executive producer on Widow's Bay , which was named Outstanding Comedy Series.

Rhys's wins also made him the first male actor to have won lead acting Emmys across drama, comedy and limited series, thanks to his 2018 win for The Americans .

But amid all the accolades, it was the actor's touching tribute to his longtime partner and The Diplomat star Keri Russell that offered a glimpse at the relationship behind one of television's most well-known power couples.

It's a love story that began more than a decade ago on the set of The Americans and has quietly continued as both of their careers have flourished.

Rhys's tribute didn't come during his acceptance speeches — Russell wasn't mentioned in his speeches. But backstage, after receiving his awards, he heaped praise on Russell, who was nominated for two 2026 Emmys herself (as a lead actress and executive producer on The Diplomat ), bringing her Emmy nominations count to eight.

Backstage after the ceremony, Rhys joked that any competitiveness between himself and Russell is "not playful." He added, "I've got a lot of money on myself. The kids ran a book, and I was the odds-on favorite. It's going to be a rough week for her. I'm sorry — I don't know if I am to be perfectly honest. You know, she's always the class act. She sends her fellow nominees Gloria Steinem quotes about being linked and not judged, and I'm the one going, 'Wahoo!'"

Rhys finished by saying that Russell was "always really the winner, if I'm perfectly honest," and added that "next year she might get one, that's my bet."

The affectionate teasing and mutual support are typical of Rhys and Russell, who have spent over a decade navigating successful careers, parenthood and awards-season competition — while keeping their love life as private as possible.

Despite appearing together on red carpets and speaking fondly about each other in interviews, the couple has never made their relationship their calling card. Instead, they've kept the focus on their individual careers — an independence that was apparent on Monday night. They are not married (in his 2018 Emmys acceptance speech, Rhys said that Russell told him she'd punch him " clean in the mouth " if he proposed) but share a home in Brooklyn, N.Y., while working and raising their children. Together, they have a 10-year-old son, Sam; Russell has two older children from a previous relationship.

Fittingly, their relationship began with the TV show that would earn them both Emmy recognition: The Americans . Playing husband and wife Philip and Elizabeth Jennings, their onscreen relationship developed into something real. Despite their attempts to keep it under wraps, their relationship became known to their colleagues early on after Russell's New York apartment was burglarized while Rhys was there.

Since then, it has unfolded as their individual careers have blossomed. Some 12 years later, they're still operating at the top of their game with The Diplomat earning Russell repeat Emmy recognition and Rhys achieving this historic three-Emmy night.

And while Rhys may have won the family bet this time around, his backstage comments made clear who he believes comes out on top.

articles.title: Voicemod’s new pocket-friendly device brings real-time voice changing to your phone
articles.summary: Voicemod’s Key Pocket sticks to the back of your phone and works alongside a mobile app and microphone to alter your voice during games, calls, or streams.
articles.body: Voicemod announced a new mobile device that expands the capabilities of the Voicemod Key dongle it launched in late 2024 as a way to bring the company’s real-time voice changing tech to consoles. While the older Voicemod Key only used a smartphone as an interface between the company’s mobile app and the Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch, the new Key Pocket can be used to change your voice or trigger sound effects while you’re playing games, making calls, or streaming on Apple or Android mobile devices. The Voicemod Key Pocket is now available as a standalone device for $99.90 or as part of a $129.90 bundle that includes the hardware and a Voicemod Pro license. The extra $30 fee gets you lifetime access to the hundreds of voices created by the company and the thousands made by the community, the ability to create your own custom voices, and cloud syncing across multiple platforms without a subscription. [Image: The Key Pocket is compatible with Android, iOS, and iPadOS devices with a USB-C port. Although Voicemod first expanded outside the PC with the introduction of Voicemod Clips on iOS and Android in 2020, the mobile app could only be used to change your voice when recording short video or audio clips you could share afterward. Privacy restrictions on mobile operating systems prevent apps from altering microphone audio and sending it to other apps. The Voicemod Key Pocket doesn’t change that. The pocket-friendly device, which can stick to the back of phones or tablets that support magnetic accessories, functions as an external audio bridge. Audio from a wired or Bluetooth microphone connected to the Pocket is altered by Voicemod’s mobile app and then made available to other apps, like Fortnite, Roblox, Discord, or the apps you use for making phone or video calls, through a short USB-C cable connected to your mobile device. With the Pro license, the app provides access to over 200 voices created by Voicemod (instead of just a small selection of constantly rotating voices for free) and more than 76,000 additional options created by the community. The Pocket features six programmable buttons that can be used to quickly swap between voices or trigger short soundboard clips, a dedicated mute button, and a customizable glowing LED dial for altering voices or adjusting volume. Like the Voicemod Key, the Key Pocket can also be used as a voice changer for the latest generation of consoles, including the Switch 2 and recent versions of the Meta Quest headset.
